minutes.headline: Parks Commission voted to open the town beach July 13 with session passes, residents only, and approved lifeguard hires.
minutes.summary: Meeting held remotely, mostly about reopening the Town Beach under COVID rules: opening and closing dates, bathroom use, capacity, pass types and pricing, and staff hiring. The commission also reorganized its officers and discussed field fees for the Phillies, a recreation Facebook page and the town charter. Several motions were voted by roll call.

public_comment.topic: Asked whether a daily pass should be called a half-day or session pass since people register for morning or afternoon slots.
Concerned that proposed session times and a morning/afternoon split cut off weekday evening swimming for workers, and that daily prices may be prohibitive.

Town-wide cleaning service estimated at a monthly charge for three cleanings per week; commission questioned whether deep cleaning is needed.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted by roll call to open the Town Beach July 13, close it to the public September 13, and end the staff season September 15.
The commission amended its pass proposal to session passes for Lunenburg residents only in 2020, with reduced rates for children and seniors and free entry for ages two and under.
The commission voted to open the beach house bathrooms to the public through a fenced gate, and to raise the chaperone age to 15 and under with an adult 18 or older.
A recommendation to appoint a beach coordinator passed; the motion to recommend hiring all seven lifeguards was made, but the result was not audible.
No change was made to Phillies field fees; the recreation director is to bring back the game schedule and practice hours at the next meeting, set for the 23rd.

why_it_matters: The vote decides who can use the Town Beach this summer and what it costs: residents only, paid by session, with morning and afternoon slots that a public commenter said could limit weekday evening swimming for workers.

The beach budget covers most salaries but not preparation costs, and the capacity cap limits pass revenue, so the reopening may draw on other park funds late in a year when most of the park budget was already spent or committed.
watch_next: Next Parks Commission meeting on the 23rd at 5:30 p.m., with the Phillies game schedule and practice hours due back.
The vice chair is to contact the finance office for budget information, and the lifeguard hiring recommendation still goes to the town manager and Selectmen.
